notes: PROVISIONAL (flowfreq, not USGS). Washington's published SIR 2016-5118 set (load_state('WA')) with one change: Peak Region 2 (NSS GC1751) adds mean basin elevation, ELEV in feet (identity), refit at every AEP by GLS on the Region 2 calibration gages with flowfreq EMA quantiles through WY2025 (tools/wa_region2_provisional.py). ELEV is significant at the 50% AEP (t = 4.1) and explains about half of the published equation's bias at the Methow; its coefficient tapers to zero by the 0.2% AEP. Every AEP is refit, not only the common floods, because mixing refit and published equations gave a decreasing frequency curve at high basins (docs/WA_REGION2_METHOW.md). Every other region is the published set. Published notes follow. Transcribed from SIR 2016-5118 ver. 1.2 (November 2017; the version history says ver. 1.2 revised Regression Regions 1 and 2 in Tables 6 and 7). Equations, n, Sp and ranges from Table 6 (report p. 36); model error variance and covariance [X^T Lambda^-1 X]^-1 from Table 7 (pp. 39-42). Table 6 and Table 7 were double-entered (hand transcription from rendered pages vs. a regex parse of pdftotext -table output): 804 cells, 0 disagreements. Every equation also reproduces the report's own Table 8 regional-regression estimates at the Table 5 gage characteristics (4,064 of 4,120 values exact at 3 significant figures, 46 more within 1%), and matches live NSS (Washington, citation 150, regression regions 717-720, codes GC1750-GC1753), whose equation strings carry the same coefficients. Equation forms: Regions 1 and 2 Q = a A^b 10^(cP) / 10^(d CAN); Region 3 Q = a A^b P^c; Region 4 Q = a A^b 10^(cP). Stored as intercept = log10(a), DRNAREA log10, PRECPRIS10 identity (log10 in Region 3), CANOPY_PCT identity with coefficient -d. PRECPRIS10 and CANOPY_PCT are NSS's codes for the report's P (PRISM 1981-2010 mean annual precipitation, Table 5 PRECIP) and CAN (NLCD 2001 area-weighted canopy, percent). Limits are Table 6's ranges; NSS's differ slightly (it rounds them: Region 1 DRNAREA max 3310 vs 3,304; Region 3 PRECPRIS10 min 33.2 vs 33.29). Units: model_error_variance is Table 7's sigma_delta^2 (log10 units squared) as printed. sep_log is Table 6's Sp (average standard error of prediction, percent) converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (Sp/100)^2)) / ln(10). The report publishes no AVP, so avp is not stored; SEM and pseudo-R2 are not stored. n_sites is Table 6's number of stations; with it evaluate() reproduces Table 7's t critical values (1.662, 1.6630, 1.6559, 1.656). Covariance: Regions 1 and 2 are taken at full precision from the report's Flood Q Tools workbook (sir20165118_floodqtools.xlsm, sheet 'Flood Q Regression Tool'), whose values round to Table 7's 4 significant figures except at three cells where Table 7 is misprinted: Region 1 AEP 0.01 (CAN, A) is printed +1.560e-5 below the diagonal but -1.560e-5 above it (workbook -1.5602854e-5); Region 2 AEP 0.5 (P, Intercept) is printed -1.276e-4 below the diagonal but -1.267e-4 above it (workbook -1.2665308e-4); Region 2 AEP 0.1 (P, P) is printed 5.287e-6 (workbook 5.2784385e-6). The workbook matrix reproduces the report's worked example (p. 43: Region 2, AEP 0.01, x'Ux = 0.00868359) exactly; Table 7's rounded values give 0.0086777. Region 3's covariance is Table 7 as printed (the workbook carries the same 4 significant figures). The row order is intercept then A, P, CAN, in the log10(A), raw P, raw CAN basis: MEV + mean x'Ux over each region's calibration gages (Table 5, 'Used in Regional Regression? = Yes') reproduces Sp^2 within 0.5% (Regions 1 and 2) and 1.1% (Region 3). Region 4's covariance is Table 7 as printed (p. 42; column header 'P (inches)', no footnote), double-entered (48 cells, 0 disagreements), in the basis [1, log10(A), P/10]: PRECPRIS10 carries scale = 0.1 and its coefficient is stored times 10 (0.004 -> 0.04 at AEP 0.01), so every Region 4 estimate is unchanged. The P/10 basis is the regression's own. (1) With P/10, MEV + mean x'Ux over the 139 calibration gages reproduces Table 6's Sp within 0.5 percent at every AEP; with raw P it is 2.6 to 2.9 times Sp, and the P coefficient would be insignificant (t about 1.3). (2) An independent GLS refit of the report's own data (tools/wa_region4_refit.py; docs/WA_REGION4_REFIT.md) puts the P variance of [X' Lambda^-1 X]^-1 at 1.2 times Table 7's printed value in the P/10 basis and 0.012 times it with raw P; the same refit reproduces Regions 1-4's coefficients and MEV (MEV within 0.89-1.13 of Table 7). The report's downstream computations nevertheless apply the printed matrix to raw P: the text (eq. 8) defines X_i as the characteristics 'as used in the regression equation', the Flood Q Tools workbook builds Region 4's row as [1, LOG10(DA), P] (cell BN4), and Table 8's WIE weighted estimates invert to a regression variance matching raw P (median ratio 0.985 over 338 Region 4 gage-AEP pairs; PR #65). flowfreq follows the regression, so its Region 4 prediction intervals are about 3 times narrower than the workbook's and its weighted estimates give the regression more weight than Table 8 does. tests/test_regression_washington.py pins both the stored basis and the report's raw-P usage. The Flood Q Tools workbook's own Region 2 DRNAREA range (0.42-1820) disagrees with Table 6 (0.42-1,322) and with NSS (1330); Table 6 is used. The workbook also gives a to more digits than Table 6 at three AEPs (Region 2 AEP 0.002 169.824; Region 4 AEP 0.005 108.893 and 0.002 134.276); Table 6's printed values, which NSS also uses, are stored. NSS labels its citation ver. 1.1 (October 2016) but its Region 1 and 2 coefficients are ver. 1.2's.
